key_insight: DomainShuttle targets open-domain subject-driven text-to-video generation, aiming to keep the subject recognizable while allowing non-essential details to change with the prompt. It is designed to support both in-domain fidelity and cross-domain flexibility.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of generating videos from text that preserve a reference subject’s identity and core traits, especially when the desired output needs to work across different domains and styles rather than only in easy in-domain cases.
method: Frames the task as open-domain subject-driven text-to-video generation with two settings: in-domain preservation and cross-domain adaptation.
Focuses on maintaining intrinsic subject features while letting subject-irrelevant attributes vary according to the text prompt.
Aims to improve on existing approaches that mostly optimize for subject fidelity in in-domain scenarios.
impact: This is useful for practitioners building controllable video generation systems that need both identity consistency and prompt flexibility. It broadens the practical use of T2V models for creative editing, personalized content generation, and domain-shifting applications.

paper_title: DomainShuttle: Freeform Open Domain Subject-driven Text-to-video Generation
paper_authors: Nan Chen, Yiyang Cai, Rongchang Xie, Junwen Pan, Cheng Chen
